title: MI Women Vs UP Women Head-To-Head: Key Players And Who Has The Upper Hand? | Cricket News - News18
text: After bagging two consecutive wins, Mumbai Indians aim for the No.1 spot in the Women’s Premier League 2026 in the match against the UP Warriorz on Thursday, January 15. MI managed to edge over the Gujarat Giants to reach the second spot after winning a high-scoring bout by seven wickets. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur led her troops valiantly, playing an imposing knock of 71* off 43 deliveries to push them over the line in a stiff chase of 193. The two-time winners are now placed behind only Royal Challengers Bengaluru, a team they conceded their opening-day loss to. As for the Warriorz, Meg Lanning & company couldn’t have conjured up a worse start for themselves at the beginning of the tournament. Having gone down to the Giants and RCB, the Warriorz also performed poorly against the Delhi Capitals, losing by 7 wickets. They now languish at the bottom of the pile, in dire need of a victory and some inspiration. The defending champions, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, have a great opportunity to climb up the top of the points table with a win against their struggling UP rivals. Mumbai Indians have historically dominated UP Warriorz in the WPL. Harmanpreet’s titleholders have faced this opposition seven times over the past three editions and won the rubber on five occasions, losing just twice. Harmanpreet Kaur: Harmanpreet has rallied her side behind her quite masterfully, showing great tactics on the field and then dominating with the bat herself. She played another terrific knock in the last game. Shabnim Ismail: The experienced bowler quietly made a big difference in the high-scoring encounter against the Giants. She delivered a tight spell of 1 for 25 off her 4 overs, ensuring the opposition couldn’t take the game away from her side. Meg Lanning: Lanning tried her best to give Warriorz a shot at victory over the Capitals, playing a free-flowing knock of 54 off 38 balls. The veteran player smashed 9 fours and 1 six, batting at a strike-rate of 142.11. Harleen Deol: The Warriorz took a surprise call to retire out Deol even as the Indian middle-order star appeared in good form. She had blazed a promising 47* off 36 deliveries, including seven fours, before the management curiously decided to call her back. It’s a battle between two teams in massively contrasting form. While the Mumbai Indians have bounced back exceptionally well from their last-ball defeat to the Royal Challengers and clinched two wins since then, the UP Warriorz have suffered a trio of losses. MI do hold the aces heading into this contest. It would be a surprise result if the Warriorz came out triumphant in this one.
